## ⚠️ Console Performance Budget — gauge not trustworthy

The eager closure was measured, but one of the ceilings it is measured against no longer means what it names, so this run carries **no pass/fail verdict** for the performance budget.

**This is not a budget violation.** Nothing grew: the half marked below is a verdict about the gauge, and a ceiling that has stopped measuring anything can neither clear a bundle nor condemn one.

| Step | Outcome |
|------|---------|
| Build packages | `success` |
| Check console performance budget | `failure` |

**Which half objected:**

| Eager-closure half | Verdict |
|--------------------|---------|
| Aggregate closure ceiling | ✅ pass |
| Per-chunk ceilings | ✅ pass |
| Ceiling sensitivity (headroom) | ⚠️ broken gauge |
| Ceiling freshness (checkout vs. base branch) | ✅ pass |

> ⚠️ A **broken gauge** half is a verdict about the ceiling, not about the bundle: that line has drifted out of range of the regression it exists to catch, or the report behind it cannot be trusted. It does not say anything grew. The `Check console performance budget` step log carries the ceiling and the number it was compared against.

Reason: The entry chunk measured 144.5 KB, but the eager-closure half of this gate returned no trustworthy VERDICT: the report could not be read, a ceiling has drifted out of range of the regression it must catch, or (objectui#6245) a ceiling was replaced on the base branch after this checkout was made. The step log says which. This is not a passing budget — and it is not a size regression either.

See the [workflow run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/34783990240) for details.

## PM pre-merge probe — `domain:devx @ objectui` seat (#5748)

⚠️ **Posted BEFORE the merge.** Re-verified at the **ACTUAL base `7098eed365`** (ERRATA 62b — ⛔ not the base the PR records).

### ⭐ Leg 1 — the ACCEPTANCE, verified with the compiler, and it is TWO-SIDED

⚠️ This defect is **latent** (the card counted **0** `.ts` consumers reading `.interpolation`, control `.comment` hitting), so 「something red went green」 was unavailable. The acceptance is a **diagnostic flip** — and ⭐ **one leg is not enough**, which is what makes this PR's proof unusually good.

Run here independently, `ts.createProgram` + `getPreEmitDiagnostics`, `allowJs: true` / `checkJs: false` / `strict`, against the pre and post copies of the module:

```
PRE  — 2 diagnostics
  L2 TS2339: Property 'interpolation'   does not exist on type '{ comment: Uint8Array; literal: Uint8Array; }'
  L4 TS2339: Property 'nosuchProperty'  does not exist on type '{ comment: Uint8Array; literal: Uint8Array; }'

POST — 1 diagnostic
  L4 TS2339: Property 'nosuchProperty'  does not exist on type '{ comment: Uint8Array; literal: Uint8Array; interpolation: Uint8Array; }'
```

- `.interpolation` — **error → clean** ✅
- `.comment` — clean on both sides (declared control)
- ⭐ **`.nosuchProperty` — STAYS TS2339**, and its message now enumerates **THREE** properties instead of two.

⭐ **Why that third line is the leg that matters:** reading `.interpolation` cleanly is *also* satisfied by a return type destroyed into `any` or an index signature. A genuinely-absent property **still** erroring is what proves the type was **WIDENED, not DESTROYED**. Both legs ran in the same run on each side. ⛔ Without the absent-property control this PR would be indistinguishable from one that broke the type entirely.

### Leg 2 — the function body is untouched

`scanSource`, declaration through its own closing brace:

| | lines | `sha256[:16]` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| pre (`7098eed365`) | 222–437 | **`8e715c3a20dc63fc`** |
| post | 226–441 | **`8e715c3a20dc63fc`** |

**Identical.** The docblock grows 4 lines, so the body shifts down — ⭐ which is exactly why the hash is bounded at the function's *own* closing brace rather than at the next declaration. (⚠️ I made that mistake earlier today on objectui#9423 and read a byte-identical function as changed.) Guard is non-empty and ⛔ not `e3b0c44298fc1c14`.

Diff on the `.mjs` is **+6/−1**, and the diff filtered to **non-comment** changed lines is **EMPTY** — docblock only.

### Leg 3 — the `@typedef` question the card raised and did NOT settle

The dispatch asked for a measurement, not a guess. The dev's answer is **NO typedef**, on a census: of **32** direct call sites, **18** destructure at the call site, **10** read one member, and ⭐ **0 bind the whole result to a name**; **0** hand-written types duplicate the shape (nonsense control 0; positive control **309** hits). A typedef needs something that must *name* the shape — an annotation, a parameter, a return elsewhere, or a duplicate to deduplicate — and all four measure zero.

⇒ it would add a second declaration site with **no reader**: the same drift class this card exists to close. ⭐ The measurement and the card's own triage comment agree independently, and a revisit trigger is recorded (a consumer that binds the whole result).

### Leg 4 — the pin test asserts the DIAGNOSTIC, not the tag's spelling

`js-comment-mask-returns-interpolation-9424.test.ts` compiles real reads against the real `.mjs` under the real project options and pins **both directions**. Ablation: reverting the tag fails the new pin in exactly the predicted split, while **objectui#9324's control pin stays 10/10 GREEN** under the same mutation — ⭐ so the red is *this tag* being load-bearing, ⛔ not `allowJs` or the harness.

⚠️ **Fixture hygiene, explicitly checked:** no comment of any kind inside any probe or pin fixture, so no `@ts-`-prefixed token can be parsed as a real directive. That fence exists because **I** wrote `// @ts-ignore-nothing` as a label earlier today and TypeScript parsed it as `@ts-ignore`, silently suppressing the diagnostic I was measuring.

### ⭐ Why this card existed at all

objectui#9324 (landed `fcdc4d0150`) named `scanSource` as its **designated control** — the already-correct function proving the missing `@param` tags on the other three were the defect rather than `allowJs` failing to type anything. Editing the control in that PR would have dissolved its own proof, so the dev filed this instead of riding it in. ⭐ That judgement was right, and it is why `scanSource`'s body hash is the *same value* in both PRs' probes.

### Reported, ⛔ not filed, ⛔ not fixed

`scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` documents a pluggable masker whose usage example stubs a `scanSource` returning only `{ comment }` — narrower than the shape just pinned. Appears deliberate (its `compareFile` reads only `comment`), but if that gate ever grows a `literal` or `interpolation` reader, the documented stub becomes a trap.

⚠️ Noted by the dev against themselves: their commit message carries a `Part of #9424` trailer against the convention that card references live only in the PR body. `Part of` closes nothing, and no-force-push means it was not amended. On the record rather than quietly fixed.

⇒ Flipping ready and enqueueing once the governed guard settles.
